hypotheses.justification: hexForm a b = a²+ab+b², and 4·hexForm a b = (2a+b)²+3b² ≡ (2a+b)² (mod 3), so hexForm is always ≡ 0 or 1 mod 3. With hp and hπ, p is therefore either 3 or ≡ 1 mod 3; h1 only excludes p = 3, which is represented (hexForm 1 1 = 3). For p = 3 the identity still holds. reprSols_mul_eq_union (needs only hp, hπ) gives reprSols (3n) = image (emul (a,b)) (reprSols n) ∪ image (emul (a+b,-b)) (reprSols n). Because 3 ramifies, all elements of norm 3 are associates, so (a+b,-b) is a unit multiple of (a,b). reprSols n is closed under unit multiplication (mem_reprSols_iff characterises it by the norm alone), so the two images coincide. card_image_emul (no h1) then gives reprCount (3n) = reprCount n. Hence reprCount (9m) = reprCount (3m) = reprCount m, and r(9m) + r(m) = 2·r(3m); for m = 0 both sides are 1+1 = 2. Proof without h1: case on p = 3. If p ≠ 3, derive p % 3 = 1 from hπ and hp via the mod-3 computation and run the existing proof; if p = 3, use the argument above. (hp, by contrast, is needed: p = 91 is represented, satisfies 91 % 3 = 1, and fails at m = 1, since 60 ≠ 48.)
